units.title: Construct: Inline bytes, allocator failure and explicit relocation
steps: Derive the representation invariant for empty, inline and heap states and the exact invalidation events for borrowed views; explain why alignment of a character array alone does not permit arbitrary typed C objects.
Implement all capacity transitions and a fixed-capacity alternative using allocator injection, with strong append rejection and exactly-once resource release under move/reset.
checks: Appending16 bytes performs no allocation. A failed17th byte preserves length16 and all bytes. Successful spill followed by move leaves the source empty and transfers exactly one allocation. Truncating to8 and compacting frees that allocation once; resetting both owners performs no second free.

Run an operation-model generator over append lengths0,1,15,16,17,127,128,129; truncate, compact, move and reset. Preserve operation traces and independent byte-list state. Inject allocator failure at every spill and verify live allocation ownership, exact release counts and output state separately from callback instrumentation. Compile without a container/string library. Record sizeof/_Alignof on each available target. The header intentionally exposes fields for teaching, so forged state is outside the checked API contract and must be discussed.
reasoning: Small-buffer optimization introduces two ownership regimes and an often-hidden object-type problem. An address satisfying alignment is not proof that a declared unsigned-char array may be accessed through any desired struct pointer.

Construct a separate fixed-capacity16-byte variant that always rejects spill. Compare its contract and owner size with struct d_small. No string terminator, generic typed placement, automatic copy constructor or raw-struct move is supplied.

units.title: Construct: Four saturating byte lanes without cross-lane carries
steps: Derive low7-bit addition, high-bit combination and saturation masks, proving which intermediate carries can occur and why neighboring lanes remain independent.
Implement the unsigned SWAR expression and an independent scalar oracle without relying on char signedness, endian memory reinterpretation or vector extensions.
checks: 0xff00ff00 plus0x01010101 produces0xff01ff01. A255+1 low lane must saturate without adding1 to the adjacent lane. Every pair of byte inputs must agree with min(255,a+b).

The supplied anchor exhausts65,536 pairs repeated across lanes and placed into each isolated lane. Extend the oracle with all neighbor lane boundaries0,127,128,255 around each active pair and100,000 seeded mixed words. Record that the exhaustive dimension is the single-lane value pair, not all2^64 word pairs. Inspect shifts against width and integer promotions. Compare little- and big-endian serialization separately from numerical results.
reasoning: Ordinary word addition is not lane-wise addition; carries and saturation require a proof. A benchmark over only identical lanes can miss a carry leaking into a different neighboring lane.
Derive low7-bit addition, high-bit combination and saturation masks, proving which intermediate carries can occur and why neighboring lanes remain independent.
deliverables: Derive and implement d_swar_add for four unsigned8-bit lanes inside uint32_t using shifts, masks and unsigned arithmetic only.
